title.title: The cotype–cotype conjecture, under the approximation property
title.subtitle: Claim: with AP, a real Banach space is K-convex exactly when $X$ and $X^*$ both have finite cotype

plain: When do a space and its mirror image both stay clear of 'spiky' shapes? Under a mild approximation rule

beats.text: Pisier: K-convexity means no copies of $\ell_1^n$ for every $n$, uniformly
One direction is classical. The converse is false without some approximation structure
Claim: the converse holds under the ordinary AP, weaker than the bounded AP conjectured

steps: Walsh transforms of finite-rank operators decay, whatever the rank
The approximation property carries that decay to the whole space
Uniform copies of $\ell_1^n$ would stop the decay: contradiction

achievement.label: Pisier's question; named by Szarek–Tomczak-Jaegermann (2009)
achievement.context: Conjectured under the bounded approximation property; proved here under the weaker ordinary one
achievement.note: False without AP, by Pisier's own construction; real scalars only

verify.detail: The equivalence under AP, with K-convexity and cotype defined from scratch. Corollaries are not
verify.ourCheck: We read the review of the Lean statement; we did not build it

voice.text: K-convex means no uniform copies of l one n. Does cotype on both sides suffice?
A decay of Walsh transforms, free of rank, rules out the uniform copies.
Claimed: yes, under the approximation property.

sources.quote: A Banach space is K-convex exactly when it does not contain $\ell_1^n$ uniformly (Pisier).

sources.ref: article, Cotype–cotype under the approximation property
sources.quote: It is false without some approximation structure, by Pisier's own construction, and was conjectured under the bounded approximation property.

sources.ref: article, Cotype–cotype under the approximation property
sources.quote: Family 326 proves it under the ordinary approximation property, which is weaker, so the result is stronger than the conjecture as posed.
AP -> (KConvex <-> FiniteCotype X and FiniteCotype X*); K-convexity, cotype, AP defined from scratch on finite sign cubes
Corollaries (entropy duality, Grothendieck pairs) not in the comparator.
